where the last inequality uses Assumption 1 (A1). Substituting (117) into (115) yields the following recursion for ‖𝑫ti‖2\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}}\|_{2}:

‖𝑫ti‖2\displaystyle\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}}\|_{2} ≤2​Lxαti−1​‖𝒙ti−2‖2+2​Lx​Lμ+Lx​δi−1​‖𝑫ti−1‖2+2​Lx​σti−1δi−1​αti−1​‖𝒛i−1‖2+Lt\displaystyle\leq\frac{2L_{x}}{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}\|_{2}+2L_{x}L_{\mu}+L_{x}\delta_{i-1}\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{i-1}}\|_{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}L_{x}\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}{\sqrt{\delta_{i-1}}\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}\|{\bm{z}}_{i-1}\|_{2}+L_{t}
≤∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​(2​Lxαtm​‖𝒙tm−1‖2+2​Lx​Lμ+Lt+2​Lx​σtmδm​αtm​‖𝒛m‖2).\displaystyle\leq\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\bigg(\frac{2L_{x}}{\alpha_{t_{m}}}\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}\|_{2}+2L_{x}L_{\mu}+L_{t}+\frac{\sqrt{2}L_{x}\sigma_{t_{m}}}{\sqrt{\delta_{m}}\alpha_{t_{m}}}\|{\bm{z}}_{m}\|_{2}\bigg). (118)

By taking expectation, we get

𝔼⁡[‖𝑫ti‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}}\|_{2}^{2}] ≲3​𝔼​[(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​‖𝒙tm−1‖2)2]+3​(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​(2​Lx​Lμ+Lt))2\displaystyle\lesssim 3\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}\|_{2}\Big)^{2}\Big]+3\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}(2L_{x}L_{\mu}+L_{t})\Big)^{2}
+3​𝔼​[(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​2​Lx​σtmδm​αtm​‖𝒛m‖2)2].\displaystyle\qquad+3\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\frac{\sqrt{2}L_{x}\sigma_{t_{m}}}{\sqrt{\delta_{m}}\alpha_{t_{m}}}\|{\bm{z}}_{m}\|_{2}\Big)^{2}\Big]. (119)

We now estimate each of the three terms on the right-hand side of (119).

For the first term, by Cauchy-Schwarz and the moment bound 𝔼⁡[‖𝒙tm−1‖22]=O⁡(1)\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}\|_{2}^{2}]=O(1), we have

𝔼⁡[(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​‖𝒙tm−1‖2)2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}\|_{2}\Big)^{2}\Big] ≤𝔼⁡[∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​‖𝒙tm−1‖22]\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}\|_{2}^{2}\Big]
≤11−Lx​δ​∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​𝔼​[‖𝒙tm−1‖22]\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{1-L_{x}\delta}\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}\|_{2}^{2}]
≲(11−Lx​δ)2=O⁡(1),\displaystyle\lesssim\Big(\frac{1}{1-L_{x}\delta}\Big)^{2}=O(1),

for sufficiently small δ\delta such that Lx​δ≤1/2L_{x}\delta\leq 1/2. For the second term, we have

(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​(2​Lx​Lμ+Lt))2≤(2​Lx​Lμ+Lt)2(1−Lx​δ)2=O⁡(1).\displaystyle\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}(2L_{x}L_{\mu}+L_{t})\Big)^{2}\leq\frac{(2L_{x}L_{\mu}+L_{t})^{2}}{(1-L_{x}\delta)^{2}}=O(1).

For the third term, since 𝒛m∼𝒩⁡(𝟎,𝑰d){\bm{z}}_{m}\sim\mathcal{N}({\bm{0}},{\bm{I}}_{d}) are independent standard Gaussian vectors, we have 𝔼⁡[‖𝒛m‖22]=d\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{z}}_{m}\|_{2}^{2}]=d. Applying Cauchy-Schwarz yields

𝔼⁡[(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​2​Lx​σtmδm​αtm​‖𝒛m‖2)2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\frac{\sqrt{2}L_{x}\sigma_{t_{m}}}{\sqrt{\delta_{m}}\alpha_{t_{m}}}\|{\bm{z}}_{m}\|_{2}\Big)^{2}\Big] ≤𝔼⁡[∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​(∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​2​Lx2​σtm2δm​αtm2​‖𝒛m‖22)]\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\Big(\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\frac{2L_{x}^{2}\sigma_{t_{m}}^{2}}{\delta_{m}\alpha_{t_{m}}^{2}}\|{\bm{z}}_{m}\|_{2}^{2}\Big)\Big]
≤11−Lx​δ​∑m=1i−1(Lx​δ)i−m−1​2​d​Lx2​σtm2δm​αtm2=O⁡(1δ),\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{1-L_{x}\delta}\sum_{m=1}^{i-1}(L_{x}\delta)^{i-m-1}\frac{2dL_{x}^{2}\sigma_{t_{m}}^{2}}{\delta_{m}\alpha_{t_{m}}^{2}}=O\Big(\frac{1}{\delta}\Big),

where we have used the assumption that max⁡δi/min⁡δi=O⁡(1)\max\delta_{i}/\min\delta_{i}=O(1). Combining the above three estimates into (119) yields

𝔼⁡[‖𝑫ti‖22]=O⁡(1δ).\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}}\|_{2}^{2}]=O\Big(\frac{1}{\delta}\Big). (120)

Finally, substituting (120) into (117), we obtain

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−2‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}\|_{2}^{2}] ≤16​δi−12​𝔼​[‖𝒙ti−2‖22]+16​αti−12​δi−12​Lμ2+4​αti−12​δi−14​𝔼​[‖𝑫ti−1‖22]+8​σti−12​δi−1​𝔼​[‖𝒛i−1‖22]\displaystyle\leq 16\delta_{i-1}^{2}\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}\|_{2}^{2}]+16\alpha_{t_{i-1}}^{2}\delta_{i-1}^{2}L_{\mu}^{2}+4\alpha_{t_{i-1}}^{2}\delta_{i-1}^{4}\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{i-1}}\|_{2}^{2}]+8\sigma_{t_{i-1}}^{2}\delta_{i-1}\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{z}}_{i-1}\|_{2}^{2}]
≲δi−12+δi−13+δi−1=O⁡(δi−1).\displaystyle\lesssim\delta_{i-1}^{2}+\delta_{i-1}^{3}+\delta_{i-1}=O(\delta_{i-1}). (121)
Step 2: decomposition of errors.

We are now ready to analyze the convergence rate of (17b). Repeating the arguments in (72)-(78), we obtain

𝒙ti−𝒙ti⋆\displaystyle{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}^{\star} =𝑨ti​(𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−1⋆)+αti2​(1−e−2​δi)​δi​𝑫ti+ℰti,1+ℰti,2,\displaystyle={\bm{A}}_{t_{i}}\big({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big)+\frac{\alpha_{t_{i}}}{2}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i}})\delta_{i}{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}}+\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},1}+\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},2}, (122)

where the matrix 𝑨ti{\bm{A}}_{t_{i}} is defined in (80).

For i≥2i\geq 2, we apply the Taylor expansion at (𝒙ti−2,ti−1)(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1}). From the definition of 𝑫ti{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}},

𝑫ti\displaystyle{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}} =1δi−1​(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1,ti−1)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−2,ti−2))\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}({\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1})-{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2}))
=1δi−1​(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1,ti−1)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−2,ti−2))\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}({\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1})-{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})+{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})-{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2}))
=1δi−1∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤(𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−2)+1δi−1O(∥𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−2∥22)+∂∂λ𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−2)+O(δi−1).\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}})+\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}O\big(\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}\|_{2}^{2}\big)+\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2})+O(\delta_{i-1}).

Substituting the expression for 𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−2{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}} from (116) yields for i≥2i\geq 2,

𝑫ti\displaystyle{\bm{D}}_{t_{i}} =1δi−1(e−δi−1σti−1σti−2−1)∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝒙ti−2+αti−1δi−1(1−e−2​δi−1)∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−2)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}\bigg({\rm e}^{-\delta_{i-1}}\frac{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-2}}}-1\bigg)\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}+\frac{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}{\delta_{i-1}}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i-1}})\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2})
+αti−12(1−e−2​δi−1)∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝑫ti−1+1δi−1O(∥𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−2∥22)+∂∂λ𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−2)\displaystyle\qquad+\frac{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}{2}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i-1}})\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{D}}_{t_{i-1}}+\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}O\big(\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}\|_{2}^{2}\big)+\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2})
+O(δi−1)+σti−1δi−11−e−2​δi−1∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝒛i−1\displaystyle\qquad+O(\delta_{i-1})+\frac{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}{\delta_{i-1}}\sqrt{1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i-1}}}\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{z}}_{i-1}
≕ℰti,3+ℰti,4,\displaystyle\eqqcolon\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},3}+\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},4}, (123)

where the residual terms ℰti,3\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},3} and ℰti,4\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},4} are defined as

ℰti,3\displaystyle\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},3} ≔1δi−1(e−δi−1σti−1σti−2−1)∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝒙ti−2+αti−1δi−1(1−e−2​δi−1)∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−2)\displaystyle\coloneqq\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}\bigg({\rm e}^{-\delta_{i-1}}\frac{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-2}}}-1\bigg)\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}+\frac{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}{\delta_{i-1}}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i-1}})\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2})
+αti−12(1−e−2​δi−1)∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝑫ti−1+1δi−1O(∥𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−2∥22)+∂∂λ𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−2)\displaystyle\qquad+\frac{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}{2}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i-1}})\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{D}}_{t_{i-1}}+\frac{1}{\delta_{i-1}}O\big(\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}}\|_{2}^{2}\big)+\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda}{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-2})
+O⁡(δi−1),\displaystyle\qquad+O(\delta_{i-1}), (124a)
ℰti,4\displaystyle\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},4} ≔σti−1δi−11−e−2​δi−1∇𝝁θ(𝒙ti−2,ti−1)⊤𝒛i−1,\displaystyle\coloneqq\frac{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}{\delta_{i-1}}\sqrt{1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i-1}}}\nabla{\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-2}},t_{i-1})^{\top}{\bm{z}}_{i-1}, (124b)

and ℰt1,3=ℰt1,4=𝟎.\mathcal{E}_{t_{1},3}=\mathcal{E}_{t_{1},4}={\bm{0}}. Denote c1=0c_{1}=0 and ci=αti2​(1−e−2​δi)​δic_{i}=\frac{\alpha_{t_{i}}}{2}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i}})\delta_{i} for i≥2i\geq 2. Substituting (123) into (122) gives

𝒙ti−𝒙ti⋆\displaystyle{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}^{\star} =𝑨ti​(𝒙ti−1⋆)​(𝒙ti−1−𝒙ti−1⋆)+ℰti,1+ℰti,2+ci​ℰti,3+ci​ℰti,4\displaystyle={\bm{A}}_{t_{i}}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star})\big({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big)+\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},1}+\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},2}+c_{i}\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},3}+c_{i}\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},4}

where we have used the bound

αti2​(1−e−2​δi)​δi≤αti​δi2=O⁡(δi2).\frac{\alpha_{t_{i}}}{2}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{i}})\delta_{i}\leq\alpha_{t_{i}}\delta_{i}^{2}=O(\delta_{i}^{2}).

By recursion, we get the final decomposition

𝒙tM−𝒙tM⋆\displaystyle{\bm{x}}_{t_{M}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{M}}^{\star} =∑m=1M∏j=m+1M𝑨tj​(ℰtm,1+ℰtm,2+cm​ℰtm,3+cm​ℰtm,4).\displaystyle=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\prod_{j=m+1}^{M}{\bm{A}}_{t_{j}}\bigg(\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},1}+\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},2}+c_{m}\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},3}+c_{m}\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},4}\bigg). (125)

Taking expectations and applying the uniform product bound (84), we obtain

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙tM−𝒙tM⋆‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{M}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{M}}^{\star}\|_{2}] ≲∑m=1M𝔼⁡[‖ℰtm,1‖2]+𝔼⁡[‖∑m=1M∏j=m+1M𝑨tj​ℰtm,2‖2]\displaystyle\lesssim\sum_{m=1}^{M}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},1}\|_{2}]+\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Big\|\sum_{m=1}^{M}\prod_{j=m+1}^{M}{\bm{A}}_{t_{j}}\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},2}\Big\|_{2}\bigg]
+∑m=1Mδm2𝔼[∥ℰtm,3∥2]+𝔼[∥∑m=2Mcm∏j=m+1M𝑨tjℰtm,4∥2].\displaystyle\qquad+\sum_{m=1}^{M}\delta_{m}^{2}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},3}\|_{2}]+\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Big\|\sum_{m=2}^{M}c_{m}\prod_{j=m+1}^{M}{\bm{A}}_{t_{j}}\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},4}\Big\|_{2}\bigg]. (126)
Step 3: control each term separately.

We now bound the four terms on the right-hand side of (126) separately.

  • •

    Bounding the first term. We aim to establish

    ∑m=1M𝔼⁡[‖ℰtm,1‖2]=O⁡(δ),\displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{M}\mathbb{E}[\|\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},1}\|_{2}]=O(\delta), (127)

    Recalling the analysis in Step 4 of Section C.1, it suffices to prove the second-moment bound

    𝔼⁡[‖𝒙tm−𝒙tm⋆‖22]=O⁡(δ).\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}^{\star}\|_{2}^{2}]=O(\delta).

    To this end, we repeat the arguments leading to (101), which now include the additional drift-difference term:

    ‖𝒙tm−𝒙tm⋆‖2\displaystyle\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}^{\star}\|_{2} ≤σtmσtm−1​e−δm​‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖2+αtmαtm−1​Lx​(1−e−2​δm)​‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖2\displaystyle\leq\frac{\sigma_{t_{m}}}{\sigma_{t_{m-1}}}{\rm e}^{-\delta_{m}}\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}+\frac{\alpha_{t_{m}}}{\alpha_{t_{m-1}}}L_{x}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{m}})\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}
    +2​Btm+12​δm​αtm​(1−e−2​δm)​‖𝑫tm‖2,\displaystyle\qquad+2B_{t_{m}}+\frac{1}{2}\delta_{m}\alpha_{t_{m}}(1-{\rm e}^{-2\delta_{m}})\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{m}}\|_{2}, (128)

    where BtmB_{t_{m}} is defined in (102). Repeating the derivation of (105), we obtain

    𝔼⁡[‖𝒙tm−𝒙tm⋆‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}^{\star}\|_{2}^{2}] ≤(1+2​αtm​Lx​δmαtm−1)2​𝔼​[‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖22]\displaystyle\leq\big(1+\frac{2\alpha_{t_{m}}L_{x}\delta_{m}}{\alpha_{t_{m-1}}}\big)^{2}\mathbb{E}\big[\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}^{2}\big]
    +2​(1+2​αtm​Lx​δmαtm−1)​𝔼​[(2​Btm+O⁡(δm2)​‖𝑫tm‖2)​‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖2]+𝔼⁡[(2​Btm+O⁡(δm2)​‖𝑫tm‖2)2]\displaystyle\qquad+2\big(1+\frac{2\alpha_{t_{m}}L_{x}\delta_{m}}{\alpha_{t_{m-1}}}\big)\mathbb{E}\big[(2B_{t_{m}}+O(\delta_{m}^{2})\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{m}}\|_{2})\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}\big]+\mathbb{E}[(2B_{t_{m}}+O(\delta_{m}^{2})\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{m}}\|_{2})^{2}]
    ≤(a)​(1+2​αtm​Lx​δmαtm−1)2​𝔼​[‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖22]\displaystyle\overset{\text{(a)}}{\leq}\big(1+\frac{2\alpha_{t_{m}}L_{x}\delta_{m}}{\alpha_{t_{m-1}}}\big)^{2}\mathbb{E}\big[\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}^{2}\big]
    +2​(1+2​αtm​Lx​δmαtm−1)​O​(δm1.5)​𝔼⁡[‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖22]+O⁡(δm3)\displaystyle\qquad+2\big(1+\frac{2\alpha_{t_{m}}L_{x}\delta_{m}}{\alpha_{t_{m-1}}}\big)O(\delta_{m}^{1.5})\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\big[\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}^{2}\big]}+O(\delta_{m}^{3})
    ≤​(1+5​αtm​Lx​δmαtm−1+O⁡(δm))​𝔼​[‖𝒙tm−1−𝒙tm−1⋆‖22]+O⁡(δm2),\displaystyle\overset{\text{}}{\leq}\big(1+\frac{5\alpha_{t_{m}}L_{x}\delta_{m}}{\alpha_{t_{m-1}}}+O(\delta_{m})\big)\mathbb{E}\big[\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m-1}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}^{2}\big]+O(\delta_{m}^{2}), (129)

    where (a) holds since

    𝔼⁡[(2​Btm+O⁡(δm2)​‖𝑫tm‖2)2]≲𝔼⁡[Btm2]+δm4​𝔼​[‖𝑫tm‖22]=O⁡(δm3).\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[(2B_{t_{m}}+O(\delta_{m}^{2})\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{m}}\|_{2})^{2}]\lesssim\mathbb{E}[B_{t_{m}}^{2}]+\delta_{m}^{4}\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{D}}_{t_{m}}\|_{2}^{2}]=O(\delta_{m}^{3}).

    By recursion, we have

    𝔼⁡[‖𝒙tm−𝒙tm⋆‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{m}}^{\star}\|_{2}^{2}] ≲∑i=1mexp⁡(∑j=i+1m(5​αtj​Lx​δjαtj−1+O⁡(δj)))​δi2=O⁡(δ).\displaystyle\lesssim\sum_{i=1}^{m}\exp\Big(\sum_{j=i+1}^{m}\big(\frac{5\alpha_{t_{j}}L_{x}\delta_{j}}{\alpha_{t_{j-1}}}+O(\delta_{j})\big)\Big)\delta_{i}^{2}=O(\delta). (130)

    This establishes (127).

  • •

    Bounding the second term. Recall the definition of ℰtm,2\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},2} (cf. (79b)), which is independent of the update rule for 𝒙ti{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}.Therefore, the analysis in Appendix C.1 remains valid, and we have

    𝔼⁡[‖∑m=1M∏j=m+1M𝑨tj​ℰtm,2‖2]=O⁡(δ).\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\bigg[\Big\|\sum_{m=1}^{M}\prod_{j=m+1}^{M}{\bm{A}}_{t_{j}}\mathcal{E}_{t_{m},2}\Big\|_{2}\bigg]=O(\delta). (131)

    Bounding the third term. For the definition of ℰti,3\mathcal{E}_{t_{i},3} (cf. (124a)), we have

Appendix E Proof of convergence order upper bound for F-DDIM (Theorem 4)

We write δ=maxi∈[M]⁡δi=O⁡(M−1)\delta=\max_{i\in[M]}\delta_{i}=O(M^{-1}). To establish Theorem 4, we first consider the convergence order of the following (idealized) first-order forward-value discretization of the diffusion ODE (12a). For each iteration i=1,…,Mi=1,\dots,M, given the current iterate 𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}} at time ti−1t_{i-1}, we compute the next iterate 𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}} by

𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}} =σtiσti−1​𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋+(αti−σti​αti−1σti−1)​𝝁θ​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti).\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}+\Big(\alpha_{t_{i}}-\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\Big)\bm{\mu}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}},{t_{i}}). (167)

For comparison, the deterministic DDIM update (13) can be written in the data-prediction form as

𝒙ti𝖻𝖼𝗄\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{bck}} =σtiσti−1​𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+(αti−σti​αti−1σti−1)​𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄,ti−1).\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\Big(\alpha_{t_{i}}-\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\Big)\bm{\mu}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}},{t_{i-1}}). (168)

The only difference between (167) and (168) is whether the data prediction model 𝝁θ​(𝒙,t){\bm{\mu}}_{\theta}(\bm{x},t) is evaluated at the next state/time (𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti)(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i}), or the current state/time (𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄,ti−1)(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}},t_{i-1}). As a note, while the update rule of the naive forward-value discretization (167) is not directly implementable, it serves as a clean lens for understanding how evaluation placement affects discretization error.

Interestingly, it turns out that the first-order discretization errors introduced by these two strategies have exactly opposite signs, as formalized in the following theorem. The proof is postponed to Section E.1.

Theorem 6.

Under Assumption 1, the idealized forward-value discretization scheme (167) has convergence order 11. Moreover, let 𝐱tM𝖿𝗈𝗋\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{for}} and 𝐱tM𝖻𝖼𝗄\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{bck}} denote the outputs of the forward-value discretization (167) and DDIM (168), respectively, and let 𝐱tM⋆{\bm{x}}_{t_{M}}^{\star} be the exact ODE solution defined in (28), with the common initialization 𝐱t0𝖻𝖼𝗄=𝐱t0𝖿𝗈𝗋=𝐱t0⋆\bm{x}_{t_{0}}^{\mathsf{bck}}=\bm{x}_{t_{0}}^{\mathsf{for}}={\bm{x}}_{t_{0}}^{\star}. Then we have

‖𝒙tM𝖻𝖼𝗄−𝒙tM⋆+𝒙tM𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙tM⋆‖2=O⁡(1/M2).\displaystyle\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{bck}}-\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\star}+\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\star}\big\|_{2}=O(1/M^{2}). (169)

Theorem 6 implies that the leading O⁡(1/M)O(1/M) errors of the forward-value and backward-value discretizations cancel to second order:

𝒙tM𝖻𝖼𝗄−𝒙tM⋆≈−(𝒙tM𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙tM⋆).\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{bck}}-\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\star}\approx-(\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\star}).

Conceptually, this suggests that if one can (even approximately) access forward-value information, then combining it with the standard backward-value update can greatly reduce the most harmful part of the discretization error.

Next, we provide the convergence guarantee of the proposed sampler in Theorem 7 below; with proof postponed to Section E.2.

This theorem guarantees that lookahead errors satisfying (170) are sufficiently small for the implemented method to inherit the first-order rate of the idealized forward-value scheme. E.1 Proof of Theorem 6

Proof for the first-order forward-value discretization scheme.

By the diffusion ODE with the data prediction model (see (173)), for each i∈[M]i\in[M], we can express 𝒙ti⋆\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star} in terms of 𝒙ti−1⋆\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star} as

𝒙ti⋆=σtiσti−1​𝒙ti−1⋆+σti​∫λti−1λtieλ​𝝁θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t⁡(λ))​𝑑λ.\displaystyle\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}=\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}+\sigma_{t_{i}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\mathrm{e}^{\lambda}\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda. (177)

Combining this identity with the forward-value discretization (167), we can decompose the distance between the iterates 𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}} and 𝒙ti⋆\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star} as

=σtiσti−1​(𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti−1⋆)+σti​∫λti−1λtieλ​𝑑λ⋅(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti))\displaystyle=\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big)+\sigma_{t_{i}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{\lambda}\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\cdot\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)\Big)
+σti∫λti−1λtieλ(𝝁θ(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−𝝁θ(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t(λ)))dλ.\displaystyle\quad+\sigma_{t_{i}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{\lambda}\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda. (178)

Let us control the last two terms on the right-hand-side of (178) separately. For the second term, we can leverage the Lipschitz property of 𝝁θ​(𝒙,t)\bm{\mu}_{\theta}(\bm{x},t) with respect to 𝒙\bm{x} (see Assumption 1 (A2)) to derive

‖σti​∫λti−1λtieλ​𝑑λ⋅(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti))‖\displaystyle\bigg\|\sigma_{t_{i}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{\lambda}\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\cdot\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)\Big)\bigg\| ≤σti​eλti​δi​Lxαti​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖\displaystyle\leq\sigma_{t_{i}}{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\delta_{i}\frac{L_{x}}{\alpha_{t_{i}}}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\|
=δi​Lx​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖,\displaystyle=\delta_{i}L_{x}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\|, (179)

where we used λti−1≤λti\lambda_{t_{i-1}}\leq\lambda_{t_{i}} and λt=log⁡(αt/σt)\lambda_{t}=\log(\alpha_{t}/\sigma_{t}). Similarly, we can control the third term by the total-derivative bound L~t\widetilde{L}_{t} along the exact ODE trajectory:

‖σti​∫λti−1λtieλ​(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t⁡(λ)))​𝑑λ‖\displaystyle\bigg\|\sigma_{t_{i}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{\lambda}\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\bigg\| ≤σti​eλti​∫λti−1λtiL~t​(λti−λ)​𝑑λ=12​σti​eλti​L~t​δi2\displaystyle\leq\sigma_{t_{i}}{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\widetilde{L}_{t}(\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda=\frac{1}{2}\sigma_{t_{i}}{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\widetilde{L}_{t}\delta_{i}^{2}
=12​αti​L~t​δi2=O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\alpha_{t_{i}}\widetilde{L}_{t}\delta_{i}^{2}=O(M^{-2}), (180)

where the last step arises from the condition that δi=O⁡(M−1)\delta_{i}=O(M^{-1}). Substituting (179) and (180) into (178), we find that for each i∈[M]i\in[M],

‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖≤σtiσti−1​‖𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti−1⋆‖+Lx​δi​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖+O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\|\leq\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+L_{x}\delta_{i}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\|+O(M^{-2}), (181)

or equivalently,

‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖\displaystyle\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\| ≤σtiσti−1​(1−Lx​δi)​‖𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti−1⋆‖+O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle\leq\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}(1-L_{x}\delta_{i})}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+O(M^{-2}), (182)

where the last step arises from the fact that 1−Lx​δi=1−O⁡(1/M)≍11-L_{x}\delta_{i}=1-O(1/M)\asymp 1.

Applying (182) recursively allows us to bound the final error as

‖𝒙tM𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙tM⋆‖\displaystyle\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{M}}^{\star}\big\| ≤O⁡(M−2)​∑i=1M∏j=i+1Mσtjσtj−1​(1−Lx​δj)=O⁡(M−1).\displaystyle\leq O(M^{-2})\sum_{i=1}^{M}\prod_{j=i+1}^{M}\frac{\sigma_{t_{j}}}{\sigma_{t_{j-1}}(1-L_{x}\delta_{j})}=O(M^{-1}). (183)

Here, the first step holds as 𝒙t0𝖿𝗈𝗋=𝒙t0⋆\bm{x}_{t_{0}}^{\mathsf{for}}=\bm{x}_{t_{0}}^{\star} and the last step follows from

≤M​exp⁡(2​Lx​(λtM−λt0))=O⁡(M).\displaystyle\leq M\exp\bigl(2L_{x}(\lambda_{t_{M}}-\lambda_{t_{0}})\bigr)=O(M).

We used 1/(1−x)≤exp⁡(2​x)1/(1-x)\leq\exp(2x) for 0≤x≤1/20\leq x\leq 1/2, Lx​δ≤1/2L_{x}\delta\leq 1/2 for sufficiently large MM, and σtM≤σti\sigma_{t_{M}}\leq\sigma_{t_{i}}. The same argument gives maxi∈[M]⁡‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖=O⁡(M−1)\max_{i\in[M]}\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\|=O(M^{-1}). This justifies that the convergence order of the first-order, forward-value discretization scheme is equal to 1.

Proof of Claim (169).

Let us fix an arbitrary i∈[M]i\in[M]. =σtiσti−1(𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2𝒙ti−1⋆)+σti(∫λti−1λtieλ​(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−2​𝝁θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t⁡(λ)))​dλ)⏟=:𝝌1\displaystyle\quad=\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big)+\sigma_{t_{i}}\underbrace{\bigg(\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{\lambda}\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-2\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\bigg)}_{=:{\bm{\chi}}_{1}}

      where the last identity holds because

      =(𝝁⁡(λti)−𝝁⁡(λti−1))​δi−2​(𝝁⁡(λti)−𝝁⁡(λti−1))λti−λti−1​∫λti−1λti(λ−λti−1)​𝑑λ\displaystyle\qquad=\big(\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\big)\delta_{i}-\frac{2\big(\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\big)}{\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}(\lambda-\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
      =(𝝁⁡(λti)−𝝁⁡(λti−1))​δi−2​(𝝁⁡(λti)−𝝁⁡(λti−1))δi⋅12​δi2=0.\displaystyle\qquad=\big(\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\big)\delta_{i}-\frac{2\big(\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\big)}{\delta_{i}}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\delta_{i}^{2}=0.

      Given the expression in (186), combining Taylor’s theorem with the total second-derivative bound H~t\widetilde{H}_{t}, we can derive

      ‖∫λti−1λti(𝝁⁡(λti)−𝝁⁡(λti−1)λti−λti−1​(λ−λti−1)+𝝁⁡(λti−1)−𝝁⁡(λ))​𝑑λ‖\displaystyle\bigg\|\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\bigg(\frac{\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})}{\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}(\lambda-\lambda_{t_{i-1}})+\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda)\bigg)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\bigg\|

(187)

      Applying the same total second-derivative bound again, we can further bound the first term on the right-hand side of (187) as

      ‖𝝁⁡(λti)−𝝁⁡(λti−1)λti−λti−1−𝝁′​(λti−1)‖≤‖𝝁′​(λti−1)​λti−λti−1λti−λti−1−𝝁′​(λti−1)‖+H~t​δi=H~t​δi.\displaystyle\bigg\|\frac{\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i}})-\bm{\mu}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})}{\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}-\bm{\mu}^{\prime}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\bigg\|\leq\bigg\|\bm{\mu}^{\prime}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\frac{\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}{\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}-\bm{\mu}^{\prime}(\lambda_{t_{i-1}})\bigg\|+\widetilde{H}_{t}\delta_{i}=\widetilde{H}_{t}\delta_{i}.

      Substituted into (187), this yields

      ≤12​H~t​δi3+13​H~t​δi3=O⁡(M−3).\displaystyle\qquad\leq\frac{1}{2}\widetilde{H}_{t}\delta_{i}^{3}+\frac{1}{3}\widetilde{H}_{t}\delta_{i}^{3}=O(M^{-3}). (188)

      Finally, plugging (188) into (186), the first term on the right-hand side of (185) can be bounded as

      ∫λti−1λti(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−2​𝝁θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t⁡(λ)))​𝑑λ=O⁡(M−3).\displaystyle\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-2\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda=O(M^{-3}). (189)

      Turning to the second term, one can derive

      ‖∫λti−1λti(eλ−eλti)​(𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−2​𝝁θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t⁡(λ)))​𝑑λ‖\displaystyle\bigg\|\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\big({\rm e}^{\lambda}-{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\big)\Big(\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-2\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\Big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\bigg\|
      ≤|eλti−1−eλti|​∫λti−1λti‖𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−2​𝝁θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆,t⁡(λ))‖​𝑑λ\displaystyle\quad\leq\Big|{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}-{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\Big|\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\Big\|\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-2\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star},t(\lambda)\big)\Big\|\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
      ≤eλti​δi​∫λti−1λtiL~t​(λ−λti−1+λti−λ)​𝑑λ\displaystyle\quad\leq{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\delta_{i}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\widetilde{L}_{t}(\lambda-\lambda_{t_{i-1}}+\lambda_{t_{i}}-\lambda)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
      =eλti​L~t​δi3=O⁡(M−3).\displaystyle\quad={\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\widetilde{L}_{t}\delta_{i}^{3}=O(M^{-3}). (190)

      where the second inequality uses the total-derivative bound L~t\widetilde{L}_{t} along the exact trajectory.

    Controlling χ2{\bm{\chi}}_{2}. From Taylor’s theorem and Assumption 1 (A3), we can bound

    ‖𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti−1)−2​𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)−∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)​(𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2​𝒙ti−1⋆)‖\displaystyle\bigg\|\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i-1}\big)-2\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)-\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big)\bigg\|
    ≤Hx​(‖𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄−𝒙ti−1⋆‖2+‖𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti−1⋆‖2)=O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle\quad\leq H_{x}\Big(\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|^{2}+\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|^{2}\Big)=O(M^{-2}),

    where the last step follows from the first-order bounds for DDIM and the forward-value iterates. This allows us to bound 𝝌2{\bm{\chi}}_{2} as

    ‖𝝌2‖\displaystyle\|{\bm{\chi}}_{2}\| ≤∫λti−1λtieλ​(‖∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)​(𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2​𝒙ti−1⋆)‖+O⁡(M−2))​𝑑λ\displaystyle\leq\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{\lambda}\Big(\big\|\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big)\big\|+O(M^{-2})\Big)\,\mathrm{d}\lambda
    ≤(eλti−eλti−1)​(Lxαti−1​‖𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2​𝒙ti−1⋆‖+O⁡(M−2))\displaystyle\leq\big({\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}-{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}\big)\left(\frac{L_{x}}{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+O(M^{-2})\right)
    ≤eλti​δi​Lxαti−1​‖𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2​𝒙ti−1⋆‖+eλti​δi​O​(M−2)\displaystyle\leq{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\delta_{i}\frac{L_{x}}{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\delta_{i}O(M^{-2})
    =Lx​eδi​δiσti−1​‖𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2​𝒙ti−1⋆‖+O⁡(M−3),\displaystyle=\frac{L_{x}{\rm e}^{\delta_{i}}\delta_{i}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+O(M^{-3}), (192)

    Controlling χ3{\bm{\chi}}_{3}. By Taylor’s theorem and Assumption 1 (A3), we can bound

    ‖𝝁θ​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)‖\displaystyle\big\|\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big\|
    ≤‖∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆)−∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)​(𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti−1⋆)‖\displaystyle\qquad\leq\big\|\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star})-\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star})\big\|
    +Hx​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖2+Hx​‖𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti−1⋆‖2\displaystyle\qquad\quad+H_{x}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\|^{2}+H_{x}\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|^{2}
    ≤‖(∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1))​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆)‖\displaystyle\qquad\leq\big\|\big(\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1})\big)(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star})\big\|
    +‖∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)‖​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆−𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋+𝒙ti−1⋆‖+O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle\qquad\quad+\big\|\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big\|\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+O(M^{-2}), (193)

    where the last step applies (183).

    Therefore the first term is bounded by

    ≤‖∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)‖​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖=O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle\quad\leq\big\|\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big\|\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\|=O(M^{-2}), (195)

    which together with (182) leads to

(196)

    Therefore the second term in the right-hand-side of (193) is bounded by

    ‖∇𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)‖​‖𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆−𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋+𝒙ti−1⋆‖≤Lxαti−1​O​(M−2)≤Lxαmin​O​(M−2)=O⁡(M−2),\displaystyle\big\|\nabla\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big\|\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}-\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|\leq\frac{L_{x}}{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}O(M^{-2})\leq\frac{L_{x}}{\alpha_{\min}}O(M^{-2})=O(M^{-2}), (197)

    ≤eλti​δi​‖𝝁θ​(𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti⋆,ti)−𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋,ti−1)+𝝁θ​(𝒙ti−1⋆,ti−1)‖=O⁡(M−3).\displaystyle\leq{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}\delta_{i}\big\|\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star},t_{i}\big)-\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}},t_{i-1}\big)+\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\big(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star},t_{i-1}\big)\big\|=O(M^{-3}).     Putting bounds for χ1\bm{\chi}_{1}, χ2{\bm{\chi}}_{2}, and χ3{\bm{\chi}}_{3} together. Finally, combining the bounds in (191), (192), and (198), and then plugging it into (184), we find that for any i≥1i\geq 1,

    ‖𝒙ti𝖻𝖼𝗄−𝒙ti⋆+𝒙ti𝖿𝗈𝗋−𝒙ti⋆‖\displaystyle\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{bck}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}+\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\mathsf{for}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}\big\| ≤σtiσti−1​(1+Lx​eδi​δi)​‖𝒙ti−1𝖻𝖼𝗄+𝒙ti−1𝖿𝗈𝗋−2​𝒙ti−1⋆‖+σti​O​(M−3).\displaystyle\leq\frac{\sigma_{t_{i}}}{\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}(1+L_{x}{\rm e}^{\delta_{i}}\delta_{i})\big\|\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{bck}}+\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\mathsf{for}}-2\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}}^{\star}\big\|+\sigma_{t_{i}}O(M^{-3}).

Comparing the update rules of our sampler (19) and that of the idealized forward-value discretization (167), one can express the difference between their iterates as

+δi​Lx​‖𝒙ti⋆​(𝒙ti−1,ti−1)−𝒙^ti‖,\displaystyle\quad+\delta_{i}L_{x}\big\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}^{\star}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1})-\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}\big\|, (199)

Proof of F-DDIM.

Finally, we verify the lookahead accuracy of F-DDIM satisfies (170). Let

Ei=‖𝒙^ti−𝒙ti⋆​(𝒙ti−1,ti−1)‖.E_{i}=\|\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}-\bm{x}_{t_{i}}^{\star}(\bm{x}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1})\|.

We first record uniform boundedness of the iterates. Since ‖𝝁θ‖≤Lμ\|\bm{\mu}_{\theta}\|\leq L_{\mu} and σti/σti−1≤1\sigma_{t_{i}}/\sigma_{t_{i-1}}\leq 1, the corrected update gives

‖𝒙ti‖≤‖𝒙t0‖+αmax​Lμ​∑j=1iδj=O⁡(1).\|\bm{x}_{t_{i}}\|\leq\|\bm{x}_{t_{0}}\|+\alpha_{\max}L_{\mu}\sum_{j=1}^{i}\delta_{j}=O(1).

For i≥2i\geq 2, the update rule of 𝒙^ti\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}} gives

‖𝒙^ti‖≤C​‖𝒙ti−1‖+C​δ​‖𝒙^ti−1‖=O⁡(1).\|\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}\|\leq C\|{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}\|+C\delta\|\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}}\|=O(1).

The local exact trajectories are also bounded by the integral form (173). Thus there exists a ball ‖𝒙‖≤R\|\bm{x}\|\leq R that contains all these states and trajectories.

We next establish the derivative bounds of the noise predictor 𝜺θ{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\theta}. From 𝜺θ=𝒙/σt−eλt​𝝁θ\bm{\varepsilon}_{\theta}=\bm{x}/\sigma_{t}-{\rm e}^{\lambda_{t}}\bm{\mu}_{\theta}, Assumption 1 (A1), (A2), and (A4) give the following inequalities for all 𝒙\bm{x} in a fixed ball ‖𝒙‖≤R\|\bm{x}\|\leq R and λ∈[λti−1,λti]\lambda\in[\lambda_{t_{i-1}},\lambda_{t_{i}}]:

∇𝒙𝜺θ\displaystyle\nabla_{\bm{x}}\bm{\varepsilon}_{\theta} =𝑰−αt​∇𝒙𝝁θσt,\displaystyle=\frac{\bm{I}-\alpha_{t}\nabla_{\bm{x}}\bm{\mu}_{\theta}}{\sigma_{t}}, ‖∇𝒙𝜺θ‖\displaystyle\|\nabla_{\bm{x}}\bm{\varepsilon}_{\theta}\| ≤1+Lxσt≤1+Lxσti≕Kx,i,\displaystyle\leq\frac{1+L_{x}}{\sigma_{t}}\leq\frac{1+L_{x}}{\sigma_{t_{i}}}\eqqcolon K_{x,i},

Consider F-DDIM with its cached noise predictions. We have

𝒙^ti−𝒙ti⋆​(𝒙ti−1,ti−1)\displaystyle\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}-{\bm{x}}_{t_{i}}^{\star}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1}) =αti​∫λti−1λtie−λ​𝜺θ​(𝒙t⁡(λ)⋆​(𝒙ti−1,ti−1),t⁡(λ))​𝑑λ−(αti​σti−1αti−1−σti)​𝜺~ti−1\displaystyle=\alpha_{t_{i}}\int_{\lambda_{t_{i-1}}}^{\lambda_{t_{i}}}{\rm e}^{-\lambda}{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\theta}({\bm{x}}_{t(\lambda)}^{\star}({\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1}),t(\lambda))\,\mathrm{d}\lambda-\left(\frac{\alpha_{t_{i}}\sigma_{t_{i-1}}}{\alpha_{t_{i-1}}}-\sigma_{t_{i}}\right)\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{t_{i-1}}

For i≥2i\geq 2, taking norms and using the definition 𝜺~ti−1=𝜺θ​(𝒙^ti−1,ti−1)\widetilde{\bm{\varepsilon}}_{t_{i-1}}={\bm{\varepsilon}}_{\theta}(\widehat{\bm{x}}_{t_{i-1}},t_{i-1}) gives
